tldr: In September MemHub, Motif and a kernel-managed-memory paper pitched shared memory so context one agent learns stays usable by its teammates. The thread restarted Nov 9 with a replication study showing LLM agents coordinate unprompted through shared memory, then Project-M posted a local shared memory for coding agents on Nov 18.
whats_new: Loom reached Hacker News on Nov 21 as shared memory, document search and code indexing for AI agents, the second shared-memory tool for coding agents posted there in four days.
why_it_matters: Shared memory is now a research finding as well as a product category: agents that share a store can coordinate without being told to, so the store's write and visibility rules shape agent behavior, not just recall.

beats.headline: Replication study: LLM agents coordinate unprompted through shared memory
beats.summary: A locked two-implementation replication and extension frames shared memory as a coordination channel with safety stakes.

beats.headline: Project-M posts local shared memory for AI coding agents
Loom bundles shared memory with document search and code indexing

open_questions: Do Project-M or Loom define a conflict-resolution model for concurrent agent writes to shared memory?
Which shared-memory setups produced unprompted coordination in the replication study, and can access rules prevent it?
Does any shared-memory tool let operators scope which agents can read or write which entries?
take_for_builders: Before adopting Project-M, Loom or any shared store for a multi-agent team, test concurrent writes and stale reads, and log which agent read what so unprompted coordination is visible.
